title: Arbitrary base change for a projective Noetherian family
statement:
Let $S$ be locally Noetherian, let $f:X\to S$ be
projective, and let
$\mathcal G$ be a coherent
$\mathcal O_X$-module flat over $S$.
For any morphism $g:T\to S$, without a Noetherian hypothesis on
$T$, the canonical base-change map

$$
Lg^*(Rf_*\mathcal G)\longrightarrow Rf_{T,*}\mathcal G_T
$$

is an isomorphism, and both sides are perfect.
The symbols $Lg^*$ and $Rf_*$ denote the
derived pullback and
derived direct image. Here $X_T=X\times_S T$, $p:X_T\to X$ and $f_T:X_T\to T$ are the projections, and $\mathcal G_T=p^*\mathcal G$.

proof.text: By [def-pc-projective-morphism], $f$ is quasi-compact and factors through a closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$. The projection is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]; clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] makes $f$ proper, hence separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Coherence [pqf-def-coherent] gives locally a surjection $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U$ with finite-type kernel; shrinking around each point and choosing finitely many generators of that kernel gives an exact presentation $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_V\to0$. Thus $\mathcal G$ is of finite presentation and is quasi-coherent by clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]. Together with the assumed relative flatness, these are exactly the quasi-compact separated and quasi-coherent flat hypotheses of [lem-pc-rf-base-change-flat-module]. That lemma gives the isomorphism for the canonical module base-change map of [def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map] for the arbitrary morphism $g:T\to S$; it requires neither properness nor finite presentation nor a Noetherian hypothesis on $T$.

The cited projective Noetherian perfectness lemma gives that Rf_*G is perfect. By the definition of a perfect complex, this means that locally it is represented by a bounded complex of finite projective modules.

On every open $U\subseteq S$ with a strictly perfect representative $P^\bullet$ of $Rf_*\mathcal G$, each term is a direct summand of $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$, hence flat: tensoring an injection with that term is a direct summand of tensoring it with a finite free module and is injective. The local-model comparison [lem-pc-localized-pullback-perfect-model] identifies $Lg^*(Rf_*\mathcal G)|_{g^{-1}(U)}$ with the termwise pullback of $P^\bullet$ along $g^{-1}(U)\to U$. Its flat-complex computation is [lem-pc-flat-complex-derived-pullback], applicable because $P^\bullet$ is bounded and its terms are flat. If $\iota:P^j\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$ and $\pi:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}\to P^j$ satisfy $\pi\iota=1$, their pullbacks satisfy $(g^*\pi)(g^*\iota)=1$, and $g^*\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}=\mathcal O_{g^{-1}(U)}^{\oplus r}$. Thus every pulled-back term is a direct summand of a finite free module. Zero terms remain zero, so the pulled-back complex is bounded and strictly perfect. The opens $g^{-1}(U)$ cover $T$, proving perfectness of the left side by [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Its isomorphism with the right side from Step 1 proves perfectness of the right side as well.
